headline: Food webs are interconnected chains—complexity creates resilience
universal_truth: Real systems aren't linear chains but interconnected webs; complexity provides backup paths
fun_facts: A typical ecosystem food web has hundreds of interconnected feeding relationships
Removing one species can trigger unexpected cascades—wolves affect river paths through deer behavior
Most species are connected to every other species within 2-3 links
discussion_questions: What webs are you embedded in?
How does having multiple connections provide resilience?
What happens when a key node in your network disappears?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A food chain is a line: grass to rabbit to fox. But rabbits also eat clover. Foxes also eat mice. Mice eat seeds. Everything connects to everything else—not a chain, but a web. Reality is interconnected.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Chains are simple but fragile—break one link, break the chain. Webs are complex but resilient. What does this teach about system design?
cliff.prompt: Why are webs more resilient than chains?

options.text: Webs have multiple pathways—if one connection fails, others can compensate; redundancy through interconnection creates stability
options.response: Yes. In a web, removing one species doesn't break everything—energy can flow through alternative paths. Interconnection is insurance against single-point failures.

options.text: Webs are just more complicated chains
options.response: They're more complex, but the complexity provides qualitatively different resilience...

q1.title: Redundant Connections
q1.script: Webs have redundancy built in. Multiple energy sources, multiple consumers. If one path fails, others remain. This redundancy costs efficiency but buys resilience.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Redundant Connections"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Cascade Effects
q2.script: Changes in webs can cascade unpredictably. Removing wolves changed where deer grazed, which changed vegetation, which changed rivers. Complex systems have complex consequences.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Your Webs
q3.script: You exist in webs—professional networks, social circles, information sources. Having multiple connections in each provides resilience. Build webs, not just chains.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Real systems aren't linear chains but interconnected webs. Complexity provides backup paths. Build redundancy into your connections.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 256. Tomorrow, we'll explore energy moving through life. Until then, consider how interconnected your network really is.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Web Building - Diversify Connections
growTrack.activity: Map your connections in a key area—professional, social, informational. Do you have a web with multiple pathways, or a fragile chain? Where could you add connections that would create backup paths if a key relationship failed?
